events.what: Root claims a proof that the fractional-part condition 2^k·{(3/2)^k} + ⌊(3/2)^k⌋ > 2^k never occurs, fixing g(k) = 2^k − ⌊(3/2)^k⌋ − 2 for all k
events.credibility_reason: Several F5 signals together: the author is a physics PhD candidate outside the subfield (record, alphaXiv profile); the claim needs control of (3/2)^k for every k, which is Mahler-problem territory that known methods resist; about a year with no expert uptake, citation or digestion on a landmark question; the live Wikipedia article does not mention it; the only assessment is an automated Pith review saying the abstract does not even state the condition.

events.what: Li, 'Further Improvements on Waring's Problem G(k)', bounds on G(k)

judgement.doubts: Even if Root's argument were correct it would settle only the g(k) half of a bullet that also asks for G(k), so it would be a case (partial), not whole. Li 2024 predates the snapshot and cannot set the status. No searches run; the record's own evidence was enough.

corrections.why: F2+F5: the bullet asks for both g(k) and G(k), so Root's preprint is at most a case. It is also not credible: the author is a physics PhD candidate outside the field, the claim needs control of (3/2)^k for every k (a problem in the territory of Mahler's problem), there has been no uptake in about a year, and the record says the live Wikipedia article ignores it. Nothing else after the snapshot survives.
